second_order: working out and following the parrot design
theme_note: Participants turn the proposed parrot into an agreed, corrected guide and begin following it; what varies is whether they outline, grid, question, correct, clean, or place a pixel.
These passages do the recurring work of keeping a fragile parrot present; they vary between calls, individual effort, thanks, diagnoses, repair plans, loss reports, and announcements of return.

second_order: deciding what to put beside or after the parrot
theme_note: Once a parrot exists, participants decide what visible mark or next target to add: a subreddit sign, a colony, or another target; the proposals differ in scale and reception.

second_order: negotiating where the parrot and its neighbours fit
theme_note: Participants manage contested overlap by asking for truces, correcting who is attacking, proposing small moves, bargaining over a shared border, and naming a possible shift.

second_order: exchanging protection and repair with allies
theme_note: People offer, request, acknowledge, or return help across community lines; what varies is who initiates, whether the help is promised or reported, and whether it concerns the parrot, neighbour, or both.

second_order: moving shared defence talk into the ally Discord
theme_note: Participants invite defenders into Discord, report its size, ask how to enter, and route one another there; the visible Reddit record varies between invitation, glimpse, and access instruction.

second_order: celebrating and recounting partying on the canvas
theme_note: Participants mark success, thank fellow party parrots, or recount having partied on r/place; the evidence ranges from an exchange to narrow surviving titles.

second_order: showing people where the parrot is and how it is doing
theme_note: Participants ask for and supply proof, location, or explanations of visible status so others can find or understand the parrot; answers vary from an image to coordinates and a refresh diagnosis.

second_order: answering the alleged front-page change by partying and welcoming r/all
theme_note: In the room's separate April Fools episode, participants condemn the alleged algorithm change, flood the thread with parrot commands, welcome arrivals, and celebrate reaching the front page.

second_order: asking partygoers to donate for kakapo survival
theme_note: This single code is a distinct request that recruits the front-page party for a kakapo donation appeal and belongs with no other practice in the case.
Two comments turn attention outward by endorsing overwriting communist pixels or proposing an invasion of Germany; the proposed targets differ.
The surviving title records one participant editing a bot to automate defence; no other code shows this means of work.

second_order: enforcing the room's rules on an ally request
theme_note: A moderator removes an ally request for name-calling and its author repairs the request; the two turns together show enforcement and compliance without turning alliance into unrestricted speech.

second_order: blaming outsiders for damage and settling scores
theme_note: Participants attribute damage to outside groups or bots and, after closure, make a hostile claim about another side; what varies is the named culprit and whether the passage seeks repair or settles a score.

second_order: turning communist slogans into party-parrot jokes
theme_note: Participants recruit communist words, chants, destinations, and calls into parrot play; what varies is whether they build a slogan together, make a pun, direct someone to more jokes, or post a new caption.

second_order: making the five-upvote communist meme deal
theme_note: A moderator offers a subreddit change, another cuts the threshold, and the offer is accepted; this is the bounded deal that authorises the local turn.

second_order: arguing whether communist party parrot is a joke or politics
theme_note: Participants object, unsubscribe, defend humour, explain the r/place origin, police genocide jokes, accuse others of brigading or ruining the room, and finally lock the thread; positions and remedies vary sharply.

second_order: cleaning up and proposing to rebuild after r/place
theme_note: After placement ends, participants announce a successor, suggest coordinates, seek and supply the old plans, and call for rebuilding; visible action varies from archival cleanup to proposals, with no completed rebuild shown.
